newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount in nuclear technology venture.
newsitem.headline: Discount in nuclear technology venture.

text.p: Discount Investment Corp said on Wednesday it had bought with its sister company PEC Israel Economic Corp 50 percent of an Israeli government company finding civilian uses for nuclear technology.

A Discount spokesman said it would spend $8.5 million to purchase shares in Nitzanim now held by the Hevrat Ha'ovdim and to finance future development projects. Hevrat Ha'ovdim is controlled by the Histadrut labour federation.

Nitzanim was formed four years ago by the government, which controls the other 50 percent, to initiate civilian-use projects at the Nahal Soreq nuclear reactor south of Tel Aviv. It has since formed 15 start-up companies.
Unlike the top-secret nuclear facility at Dimona, in southern Israel, Nahal Soreq -- classified as a research facility -- has always been open to international inspection.

"This investment...is another step in establishing the (Discount) group in the sphere of high technology and in directing technology developed for non-civilian uses towards business applications," Discount Investment managing director Dov Tadmor said in a statement.
Discount and PEC also have a similar accord with the government arms-development authority Rafael to commercialise Rafael technology through a joint venture called RDC.
